title: Detect concurrent work on a slice across branches and worktrees

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
slicer's tracking state is per-branch, git-tracked JSON, so a slice marked
`started` in one branch or worktree is invisible to another until they merge. On
2026-09-28 two agent sessions implemented S105 at the same time in separate
worktrees — one as `--strict`, one as `--require-render` — and neither saw the
other's in-progress work; one complete, tested implementation had to be discarded
and the other superseded on `main`. The `started` status only guards work within a
single branch's state. Nothing on `start` or `next` signals that a slice is already
being worked elsewhere, so parallel agents silently duplicate a slice.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/vcs.py` — a read-only view of branches and worktrees. The allowlist
  is currently `rev-parse`, `status`, `log`, `mv`, `ls-files`; it would gain only
  read-only queries.
- `src/slicer/ops.py` and `src/slicer/cli.py` — where `start` (and possibly `next`)
  surfaces the warning.
- a test that fakes a sibling branch/worktree and asserts the warning.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `slicer start SNN` warns (stderr, non-blocking, exit unchanged) when a worktree
   or branch whose name references `SNN` already exists elsewhere in the repo.
2. `slicer start SNN` is silent when no such branch or worktree exists.
3. The new git queries are read-only and refused by `vcs._run` if off the allowlist.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Give slicer a read-only way to notice a slice is probably already being worked in a
parallel branch or worktree, and warn on `start`. A cheap first cut: check
`git worktree list` and `git branch --all` for a name that references the slice id
(the repo already uses `feature/S<id>` branches) and print a non-blocking warning to
stderr. Extend the `vcs` allowlist only for those read-only queries. Do NOT add
cross-process locking, a shared claims registry, or blocking behavior in this slice.

Product decision to confirm before building: whether `next` should warn too, and
whether matching is by branch/worktree name or something stronger. Do not infer this
from the backlog — agree it first.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer start` prints a non-blocking stderr warning when a sibling branch or
worktree names the slice id, and stays silent otherwise. The git queries stay
read-only and on the allowlist. Exit codes are unchanged.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit, once the scope question above is settled.
